result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.resource_allocation_index()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute resource allocation index for node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10948-L11011){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.resource_allocation_index(ebunch=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Resource allocation index](/assets/graphs/resource-allocation-index.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Nodes B and E are outlined in the accent color with their shared neighbors C and D filled in accent; badges give C degree 3 and D degree 2. The card sums 1 over each degree, 1/3 + 1/2, for a resource allocation index of 0.833." width="100%"} For each pair of nodes `(u, v)`, computes `Σ(1 / |N(w)|)` for all common neighbors `w`. Similar to Adamic-Adar but uses `1/degree` instead of `1/log(degree)`, penalizing high-degree common neighbors more strongly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of node pairs to compute predictions for. Each pair can use node IDs (integers) or labels (strings). If `None`, computes for all pairs of nodes that are not already connected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(u, v, index)` tuples where index is the resource allocation score. Results are returned with node IDs. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Resource allocation shares its shape with Adamic-Adar but replaces $1/\log|N(w)|$ with the harsher $1/|N(w)|$: $\mathrm{RA}(u, v) = \sum_{w \in N(u) \cap N(v)} \dfrac{1}{|N(w)|}$. The motivating picture is a unit of resource sent from $u$ to $v$ that splits evenly at each hub $w$ before arriving; a rarer hub delivers a larger fraction. That heavier hub penalty frequently edges out Adamic-Adar on social-network link-prediction benchmarks. Runs in $O(k)$ per pair. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Resource allocation uses `1/degree` instead of Adamic-Adar's `1/log(degree)`, so it penalizes a high-degree shared neighbor even more sharply -- comparing the two side by side on the same hub-and-spoke graph shows RA scoring noticeably lower: ::: {#293cc6d5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) # Star graph: node 1 is hub connected to 2-10 graph.add_node() # Hub node 1 for i in range(2, 11): graph.add_node() graph.add_edge(1, i) pairs = [(2, 3), (2, 5)] list(zip(graph.adamic_adar_index(pairs), graph.resource_allocation_index(pairs))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [((2, 3, 0.45511961331341866), (2, 3, 0.1111111111111111)), ((2, 5, 0.45511961331341866), (2, 5, 0.1111111111111111))] ``` ::: :::
